slides.0.title: Clare Valley and Eden Valley: The Riesling Duo
slides.0.subtitle: Level 1 · Module 3 · Lesson 3
slides.1.title: Clare Valley: Riesling Pioneer
slides.1.points.0: Location: 130 km north of Adelaide; altitude 400–500 m; dry continental climate
slides.1.points.1: The spiritual home of Australian Riesling — cool nights preserve bright, lime-driven acidity
slides.1.points.2: Style: bone dry, razor-sharp acidity, squeezed lime juice, slate/mineral
slides.1.points.3: Ageing potential: 10–20 years — develops petrol, toast, honey while retaining acid freshness
slides.1.points.4: Historic moment: in 2000, Clare Valley producers collectively adopted the screwcap — a global wine revolution
slides.2.title: Eden Valley: Barossa's Cooler Sibling
slides.2.points.0: Location: 400–550 m altitude within the Barossa Zone — significantly cooler than Barossa floor
slides.2.points.1: Riesling style: more floral (jasmine, blossom) and less citrus-dominant than Clare
slides.2.points.2: Also famous for Shiraz — Henschke's Hill of Grace (130+ year old vines) is from Eden Valley
slides.2.points.3: Riesling producers: Henschke, Pewsey Vale, Heggies Vineyard
slides.3.title: Clare Valley vs Eden Valley
slides.3.left.label: Clare Valley
slides.3.left.points.1: Vivid lime juice, slate, crisp acidity
slides.3.right.label: Eden Valley
slides.3.right.points.3: Altitude is the key cool-climate tool
slides.4.question: Clare Valley producers made a landmark decision in 2000 that changed the wine world. What was it?
slides.4.options.1: They collectively switched to screwcap closures — pioneering a global wine packaging revolution
slides.4.options.2: They banned the use of irrigation
slides.4.options.3: They established Australia's first GI regulations
slides.4.explanation: In 2000, almost all Clare Valley Riesling producers agreed simultaneously to switch from cork to screwcap (Stelvin) closures. This collective decision — driven by concerns about cork taint (TCA) — sparked a global debate and ultimately led to widespread adoption of screwcaps across Australia and New Zealand. It is one of the most significant moments in modern wine history.
slides.5.title: Lesson Summary
slides.5.points.0: Clare Valley: sharp lime + slate Riesling; bold acidity; birthplace of screwcap revolution (2000)
slides.5.points.1: Eden Valley: more floral Riesling + world-famous Shiraz (Henschke Hill of Grace)
slides.5.points.2: Both valleys: cool nights, high altitude, superb Riesling ageing potential (15–20 years)
